description:
Tashkent Falcons is a creative and technology-driven team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge.

We are currently a team of two members: a Full-Stack Web Developer and a UI/UX Designer. We combine technical expertise with creativity to turn innovative ideas into engaging digital experiences.

For this challenge, we are developing LEGACY — Every Machine Has a Story, an interactive digital museum dedicated to NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars.
summary: AstroEcho is an immersive educational web platform and digital museum designed to bring NASA's discarded historical equipment on the Moon and Mars back to life. Addressing the challenge of making legacy space archives accessible and engaging, the platform features a 5-in-1 interactive ecosystem: an Explore planetary map, Ghost Logs with retro-first-person spacecraft diaries, a Mission Retrofit Lab telemetry simulator, a Gap Filling engineering puzzle based on real NASA schematics, and an Artifact Vault with 3D/AR model inspection. Built for students and space enthusiasts, AstroEcho transforms silent robotic monuments into captivating stories, inspiring the next generation of space explorers.
details:
AstroEcho is a 5-tab educational web platform and interactive museum designed to bring NASA's discarded historical equipment on the Moon and Mars to life for students (ages 10-16) and space enthusiasts.

Key Modules & Features:

1. Explore: An interactive 3D map of the Moon and Mars featuring mission beacons and "Then vs. Now" visual comparisons.

2. Ghost Logs: A retro terminal providing first-person spacecraft diaries, mission logs, audio transmissions, and Polaroid archives.

3. Mission Retrofit Lab: A real-time telemetry simulator where users adjust solar panel angles, power thresholds, and thermal controls to manage spacecraft survival physics.

4. Gap Filling: A gamified engineering challenge based on real Viking Lander schematics, where users drag and drop component labels using riddle hints.

5. Artifact Vault: A browser-based 3D model inspector and mobile WebAR projection viewer for iconic space artifacts.

Tech Stack: React, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, and <model-viewer> for zero-app-install WebAR.
